warnings: ECC_MAC_PJ_OVERRIDE=0.23 pJ per MAC (M. Horowitz, 'Computing's energy problem (and what we can do about it)', ISSCC 2014, Fig. 1.1.9 'Rough energy costs for various operations in 45nm 0.9V'): the Compute category was rescaled in the evaluator from the ERT's 1.13555 pJ/MAC to MACs x this value. Every ECC PERCENTAGE in this file has a different denominator from the primary result; no saved pJ changed. ECC_OPT_METRIC=edp: a cheaper MAC can move the mapping optimum, and the mapper was NOT re-run (it prices MACs from the ERT) -- a fixed-mapping result
DEVELOPMENT RUN: one-layer (layer3.0.conv1). These numbers validate the implementation, not any architecture ranking. Layer selection is in the path and in `identity.layers`.
approximations: Interconnect energy uses Timeloop's Legacy network model with one shared 45nm wire constant and per-architecture switching terms (archs/_shared/noc.yaml); hop distance is derived by Timeloop from each level's Accelergy area. The recon arm scales the WEIGHT share of NoC energy by K/N like the other on-chip categories.
exact stored codeword count x measured DRAM refetch factor; parity + message padding; rounded up to whole DRAM words once

The baseline's DRAM cost is a PER-BIT PRICE, not extra traffic: it reads the same weight bits as the embedded arm (the decoder is on the DRAM die, so parity is corrected there and never crosses the datapath) and pays 70 pJ/bit against 40 for the bigger, indexed array (x1.7500 on the whole DRAM category, weights, inputs and outputs alike -- a per-bit cost is a property of the device, not of a dataspace). The parity accounting on this result is the array-SIZE evidence for that price, not an energy term; it charges no pJ. E_background and E_refresh grow with the array and are not modelled.

complete codeword read: every bit of every DRAM weight read that Timeloop counts is billed, message and embedded parity alike, and no K/N reduction is applied at DRAM; no external parity; physical DRAM words are ESTIMATED as bits / word rounded up once at the end (bit-proportional -- Timeloop bills per 8-bit scalar); the final chunk's tail padding is reported, not charged, as for the baseline

ECC codec (decode/correction) energy is OUTSIDE this comparison: it is charged to neither arm (Task 2: do not silently change ECC codec energy). Note that the arms would decode different numbers of codewords -- the baseline packs whole weights into a separately stored codeword, the embedded layout cuts the weight bit stream itself -- so a codec cost would not cancel; it is simply not costed until a characterised codec energy is adopted. ECC_DECODE affects the sweep figures only.
This is a fixed-mapping, DRAM-only comparison. It credits no on-chip saving to the embedded arm and makes no inference-accuracy claim about overwriting weight LSBs with parity.

facts.label: Eyeriss v1 (+8kB filter GLB)
facts.citation: Same JSSC 52(1), 2017 as eyeriss_like.  Differs from it in ONE block: the 8 kB filter allocation the paper describes -- "the remaining 8 kB (two banks of 512-b x 64-b SRAMs) of the GLB is allocated for filter weights to compensate for insufficient off-chip traffic bandwidth" -- is declared as a Timeloop storage level instead of !Nothing. Unlike eyeriss_v2_like_wglb, whose weight level is NOT in its paper, this level IS published; what is uncertain is whether a prefetch buffer should be modelled as a reuse level.  The pair BRACKETS that uncertainty: eyeriss_like is the upper bound on DRAM weight traffic (and so on the ECC saving), eyeriss_like_wglb the lower bound. Quote the pair, never one alone.

provenance.source_document: Chen, Krishna, Emer, Sze, IEEE JSSC 52(1), 2017 -- same paper as eyeriss_like

filter_glb.quote: "Even though it is not required by the dataflow, the remaining 8 kB (two banks of 512-b x 64-b SRAMs) of the GLB is allocated for filter weights to compensate for insufficient off-chip traffic bandwidth. While the PE array is working on a processing pass, the GLB preloads the filters used by the next processing pass."
filter_glb.modelled: depth 1024 (2 x 512), width 64, n_banks 2, datawidth 8 -> 8192 weights
filter_glb.rationale: The CAPACITY and the BANK GEOMETRY are published exactly; what is a judgement call is whether a double-buffered prefetch store should be declared as a Timeloop reuse level. Modelled as a reuse level here and as !Nothing in eyeriss_like, so the two BRACKET the answer instead of one of them silently choosing it.
filter_glb.why_it_matters: eyeriss_like refetches resnet18's weights 7.0x from DRAM against 1.0-2.3x for every other design, and the ECC saving is very nearly 0.3125 * E_dram_weights / (total + 0.3125 * E_dram_weights). So this single structural choice sets the largest saving in the study. It is the reason this variant exists.

mapper_settings.seed_note: timeloop-mapper v4 exposes no random seed; pytimeloop's Mapper spec has no `random_seed` attribute. ECC_MAPPER_SEED is RECORDED so a result says which value was asked for, but it does not make the search deterministic. What does bound it is the thread count and victory condition, both of which are in the fingerprint -- so pin ECC_MAPPER_THREADS for a reproducible run rather than leaving it at 'all cores', which differs per machine.
